land.text: the Duchy of Estonia (Harria and Vironia, Reval), which 'became split' between a pro-Danish and a pro-German party after the king's death

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Denmark's heartland under Kingdom of Denmark throughout (87,067 km2 in 1333-1343); this row holds only the Estonian province and later a sliver of southern Jutland.

land.text: Estonia (Harria and Vironia), sold for 19,000 Cologne marks; sovereignty shifted on 1 November 1346

successors.note: Cliopatria's Teutonic shape adds the Estonian cells in 1352.

land.text: the southern Jutland land, back with the kingdom

successors.note: Reading of Cliopatria's 1344-1351 sliver; the pages opened do not say whose it was or how it came back.

capitals.name: Reval (Tallinn)
capitals.note: 'The capital of Danish Estonia was Reval (Tallinn), founded at the place of Lindanise after the invasion of 1219.' The southern Jutland sliver of 1344-1351 has no seat on the pages opened.

correction.text: the Duchy of Estonia (Harria and Vironia) in August 1332

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In August 1332, King Christopher II of Denmark died, and Denmark fell into political turmoil'; the Estonian province 'became split between a pro-Danish party led by Bishop of Reval, Olaf of Roskilde' and a pro-German party. Cliopatria's first shape (the Estonian province) starts in 1333; it is used for 1332 as well.

correction.text: valid for 1333-1343 as drawn; the Order held Reval and Wesenberg castles from 16 May 1343 (contested)

keyframe_review.note: 13,776 km2 for 1333-1343: Estonia (60 of its 228 cells), the province of Harria and Vironia, which the page says was ceded back to the Danish king in 1238 (Treaty of Stensby, 7 June 1238); the page gives no area, but Harju, Lääne-Viru and Ida-Viru together are about 11,000 km2, within a factor of two. Right to 1343, when 'the castles in Reval and Wesenberg were handed over to the Order by the pro-German party on 16 May 1343' (after the St George's Night Uprising of 1343); Denmark's sovereignty ended only on 1 November 1346 (sale for 19,000 Cologne marks), so the Estonian shape also holds 1344-1346 (see the 1344 verdict).

correction.text: the Jutland sliver plus the Duchy of Estonia, for 1344-1346; from 1347 the Jutland sliver alone

keyframe_review.note: 4,720 km2: twelve cells in southern Jutland (Syddanmark, between 54.7 and 55.6 N), not covered by the pages opened. The Christopher II page says only that 'for the next eight years' after his death 'it was subdued by various mortgagees' and that 'Count Gerhard took all of Jutland as his personal property' (undated); unverified: page budget, so the sliver is kept for 1344-1351. The Estonian province is added for 1344-1346: the governor list runs to Stigot Andersson (1344-1346) and the sale to the Teutonic Order took effect on 1 November 1346.

region.text: the Duchy of Estonia (Harria and Vironia)

ledger.note: 2 August 1332: Christopher II dies and the Danish crown's lands pass to mortgagees. He 'died on 2 August 1332 at Nykøbing Castle'; 'Upon his death Denmark ceased being a formal kingdom, and for the next eight years it was subdued by various mortgagees'. The Estonian province split between a pro-Danish and a pro-German party (Danish Estonia page). Cliopatria draws only the Estonian province for this row.

region.text: Danish Estonia: Harria and Vironia, with Reval and Wesenberg

ledger.note: 16 May 1343: the Order takes the castles of Reval and Wesenberg. 'The castles in Reval and Wesenberg were handed over to the Order by the pro-German party on 16 May 1343', after the Estonians of Harria rebelled in the St George's Night Uprising of 1343; the castle at Narva followed in 1345.

1 November 1346: the contest ends with the sale. 'In 1346, Estonia (Harria and Vironia) was sold for 19,000 Cologne marks to the Teutonic Order'; 'The shift of sovereignty from Denmark to the Teutonic Order took place on 1 November 1346.'

1 November 1346: Denmark's king sells Estonia to the Teutonic Order. 'In 1346, Estonia (Harria and Vironia) was sold for 19,000 Cologne marks to the Teutonic Order'; sovereignty shifted on 1 November 1346. The page names the Teutonic Order and does not mention a transfer to the Livonian branch.

1351: Cliopatria's last Danish Magnates shape ends. The pages opened say nothing about the southern Jutland sliver of 1344-1351 or its end; the land is read as back with the kingdom, as the Kingdom of Denmark row continues in 1352.

wars.name: Danish interregnum (mortgagees)
wars.outcome: 'Upon his death Denmark ceased being a formal kingdom, and for the next eight years it was subdued by various mortgagees': Count Gerhard took Jutland and Count Johan Funen and Zealand 'as his personal property' (undated).
wars.note: The page names no Waldemar IV accession date; 1340 is only the end of the 'eight years'. Denmark's heartland is drawn in the Kingdom of Denmark row.

wars.name: St George's Night Uprising
wars.outcome: After the rising of 1343 the Order took the castles of Reval and Wesenberg (16 May 1343) and Narva (1345); Denmark sold Estonia to the Order in 1346.
wars.note: The page does not say that Denmark regained control after the uprising; its governor list runs to Stigot Andersson (1344-1346).

certainty.note: The Estonian province's inland frontier and the southern Jutland sliver are approximate; the Treaty of Stensby (7 June 1238) had fixed Harria and Vironia as the king's duchy.

sources.title: Christopher II of Denmark
sources.note: Death 2 August 1332 and the 'eight years' of mortgagees; nothing on Estonia, 1340, or 1344-1351.

sources.title: Danish Estonia
sources.note: 1332 split, 1343 uprising and 16 May 1343 handover, sale of 1 November 1346, Stensby 1238, Reval as capital; no area.

notes: Not the same state as modern Denmark: Cliopatria gives 'Danish Magnates' and 'Denmark' (1945-2024) the same Wikidata id Q350186 (listed in data/README.md as a shared id), but the modern Denmark row is 1945-2024 and unrelated; the 1333-1351 row is the Danish interregnum's fragment, a member of the umbrella (Kingdom of Denmark), and its dossier is kept separate from both Kingdom of Denmark (936-1406) and the modern Denmark. What the row is: the Estonian province 1333-1343 and a 4,720 km2 sliver of southern Jutland 1344-1351 (unverified: page budget; the Christopher II page says only that Gerhard took Jutland and Johan Funen and Zealand, undated). The Estonian province was Danish until 1 November 1346, so 1344-1346 is added by correction; Cliopatria draws Estonia in no row for 1344-1351. Gaps: the pages opened give no date for Waldemar IV's accession (1340) or for the end of the mortgagee regime, nothing on Scania's pledge to Sweden, Bornholm or Gerhard III's death; the governor list on the Danish Estonia page (Konrad Preen 1340 - May 1343, Stigot Andersson 1344-1346) was not used beyond the dates. The Livonian Order page says the Livonian order bought Estonia in 1346 and the Danish Estonia page and the State of the Teutonic Order page say the Teutonic Order did; the dossier follows the sale pages (counterpart teutonic-order). Pages: 2 opened (budget 2).
